$comment: ProofGate config — every key is optional. Drop this at your repo root as proofgate.json. Without it, ProofGate auto-detects your stack (pnpm/npm/yarn/bun, Cargo, Go, Python, Gradle/Maven, .NET, Ruby, PHP, Elixir, Deno). Read with jq, node, or python3 — whichever exists (zero hard dependency).

commands.$comment_e2e: e2e is not run by the gate — its PRESENCE is what tells ProofGate that E3 (the real flow, driven on a real runtime) is producible on this machine. Without it, and without smoke[], the gate reports max_achievable_level E2 rather than pretending E3 was merely skipped.

coupledFiles.reason: the embedded dev schema and the production SQL mirror must move together

$comment_impact: Blast radius (impact.sh). sensitiveGlobs/sensitiveTerms decide which diffs are L3 — the class that demands an adversarial pass. Paths are the primary signal; terms are matched word-bounded on ADDED non-test lines and need two DISTINCT hits, so one `bearer` in a comment never escalates a typo fix. backendCmd is the LSP seam: a command that reads changed paths on stdin and prints S<TAB>file<TAB>symbol<TAB>kind<TAB>line and C<TAB>symbol<TAB>file<TAB>line — with it, navigation_confidence is `high` instead of `low`.
$comment_guards: Turn a guard off, downgrade/upgrade its severity, or add repo-local guards. Guard names are the file name without the NN- prefix.
$comment_secrets: Extra escape hatches for the secrets guard: regexes to allow, plus the always-available inline `proofgate-allow` comment and the .proofgateignore fingerprint file.
$comment_smoke: Production smoke run only under --smoke. Each entry is a GET (url + optional status/expect-body-regex) OR a command (cmd, exit 0 = pass). Never put a real credential in url/headers — use a cmd that reads it from the environment.
$comment_proof: requireProof (opt-in, default false) makes the push-guard and stop-guard wait for EVIDENCE, not just a green mechanical gate: the claims ledger must carry a central claim at the level the blast radius demands. Leave it off until the team is recording claims — a gate that blocks on something nobody is producing yet gets bypassed, and bypass culture is worse than no gate.
$comment_editguard: editGuard (opt-in, default false) is the most intrusive rule here: with an OPEN bugfix hypothesis and no failing test recorded for it, editing a non-test source file is blocked. It exists because the counter-proof has to come FIRST, and 'first' is exactly what a prompt cannot enforce — by the time you are editing, the intention to write the test afterwards is completely sincere. hypothesis.strikeThreshold is how many refuted explanations a symptom may survive before the next hypothesis on it is escalated and the gate demands an adversarial pass.
$comment_memory: Project memory (.proofgate/memory.jsonl, committed). Every fact is ANCHORED to a file plus the blob hash it had when recorded, and staleness is DERIVED at read time — never stored — so there is no field to keep in sync and none an agent can flip. Decisions hold until revoked; inferences expire after ttlDiffs commits touch the anchored file; incidents never expire. agentDecisionsExpire makes an agent's own 'decision' expire like the inference it really is, so a guess cannot become permanent policy. liveGuards runs the diff guards on a file the moment it is edited (PostToolUse) instead of only at the gate — a pasted credential caught seconds later is an undo; caught at the gate it is a rotation.
$comment_experiment: experiment.sh runs a hypothesis in its own git worktree so nothing leaks between attempts — link names the dependency directories worth symlinking in rather than reinstalling per experiment.
$comment_skeptic: requireSkeptic turns 99-skeptic-required from a WARN into a FAIL: an L3 change (auth, money, migrations, crypto, permissions) cannot be called done without a recorded adversarial pass for the CURRENT commit. Leave it off until the team runs the panel — a hard block on a step nobody has wired up is how a gate gets bypassed wholesale. calibration:false stops recording which guards fire and which get suppressed; the report it feeds (verify.sh --calibration) never changes configuration on its own.
$comment_audit: audit (opt-in, off) records a CHRONOLOGY of Bash commands — not evidence. A PostToolUse hook is not handed a reliable exit code, so entries store exit:null; a log that pretended otherwise would look like evidence while being unable to tell a passing command from a failing one. Its real job is that the edit-guard can be walked around by editing through Bash and .git/ is writable: neither is preventable, both leave a trace here. Off by default because it fires on every Bash call and command lines are a likely place for a credential to sit.
$comment_hooks: The plugin's push-guard (PreToolUse) refuses `git push` without a fresh passing verdict; set pushGuard:false to disable. stopGuard (opt-in, default off) makes the Stop hook refuse 'done' without one.
